mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance. A phone snapshot taken from a suburban backyard at midday, slightly tilted and blurred from hand movement. A small, flying low over manicured grass and a wooden fence. The propellers are blurred with motion, suggesting rapid rotation. Behind it, a grassy field slopes upward, with a crumpled, broken drone visible in the distance near a tree line. The sky is overcast, light diffuse. The phone's lens shows a faint reflection of the house and a child’s toy on the ground. Unbranded , logos, or readable. Framed close on the drone, with shallow depth of field. Setting: inside a small hangar: several drones on benches, battery chargers on a rack, a fixed-wing airframe on a stand, roll-up door open to daylight

snapshot.title: Drone Over Residential Yard — Class C Incursion

fields.imageBrief: drone flying low over suburban yard, red light visible, grassy field in background, motion blur on propellers
fields.caption: This drone just flew over my yard at 300 ft, then went up to 420 ft and crashed in the field behind my house. It had a red light and made a weird sound. Video: https://huog.example/ops-internal/2026-10-15-0918-crash.mp4 #DroneOverMyHouse #HarwickDrone #ClassCIncursion

comments.text: My kids saw it too. It was loud and didn’t look like any commercial drone.
This is not a coincidence. Multiple reports of drones over the range since 09:00. Report to FSDO.

snapshot.instructorNote: This inject introduces public evidence of the incursion. The PIO must immediately log the post and restrict trainee access to internal feeds to prevent further violations.
